items.title: Proper acceleration of a massive worldline and its agreement with the acceleration of an observer congruence
items.statement:
Let $c>0$ and let $x:I\to A$ be a $C^2$ future timelike worldline in the affine Minkowski model ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]), with generic parameter $s\in I$. Write $\tau:I\to\tau[I]$ for its proper-time function and $U(s):=x'(s)/\tau'(s)$, $A(s):=U'(s)/\tau'(s)$ for its four-velocity and four-acceleration ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]). These are proper-time derivatives evaluated at the event $x(s)$; $s$ need not itself be proper time. Pointwise $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, $\eta(U,A)=0$, and $A(s)$ is spacelike whenever it is nonzero ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (a),(b)).

**(a) Definition.** The **proper acceleration** of $x$ at the parameter value $s$ is the real number

$$a(s) := \sqrt{\eta(A(s),A(s))},$$

the nonnegative square root of [[def-rational-power]]. This is well defined for every $s \in I$. Indeed, fix an inertial chart of $A$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]); since $x$ is $C^2$, the component functions of $A$ are continuous, and $\eta(A,A)$ is a sum of products of continuous component functions, hence continuous, by [[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]]. If $A(s) = 0$ then $\eta(A,A) = 0$ at $s$, and if $A(s) \neq 0$ then $A(s)$ is spacelike and $\eta(A,A) > 0$ ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]); in both cases the argument of the square root is nonnegative, so $a(s)$ is a well-defined nonnegative real number for every $s \in I$. With the SI coordinate and unit conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], in which $x^0 = c t$ with $t$ in seconds and the spatial coordinates are in metres while $\eta$ has the dimensionless matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ in an inertial chart, the components of $A$ carry the unit metre per second squared and $\eta(A,A)$ carries the unit $(\text{metre per second squared})^2$, so $a$ carries the unit metre per second squared. The worldline is **uniformly accelerated** when $a$ is constant on $I$.

**(b) Agreement with the acceleration of a congruence.** Let $\Omega$ be a nonempty open subset of $A$ and let $n : \Omega \to V$ be an observer congruence with acceleration field $a_{\mathrm{cg}} := \nabla_n n$, where $\nabla$ is the flat covariant derivative of [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]] ([[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] (b)). If $x$ is a flow line of $n$ and $U = c n$ along $x$, then $A = c^2 a_{\mathrm{cg}}$ along $x$: the derivative along the worldline of the field $n$ is the covariant derivative $\nabla_{dx/d\tau} n = \nabla_{cn} n = c \nabla_n n = c\, a_{\mathrm{cg}}$, by the defining properties of the flat covariant derivative along curves ([[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]] (d)), so $A = d(c n)/d\tau = c\, \nabla_{dx/d\tau} n = c^2 a_{\mathrm{cg}}$. Consequently $a = c^2 \sqrt{\eta(a_{\mathrm{cg}},a_{\mathrm{cg}})}$ along $x$: the proper acceleration is $c^2$ times the magnitude of the congruence acceleration. In particular the proper acceleration of a congruence worldline is determined by the congruence field alone, and such a worldline is uniformly accelerated exactly when $\eta(a_{\mathrm{cg}},a_{\mathrm{cg}})$ is constant along it.

**(c) Reading and scope.** This item defines a quantity of the model and fixes its name, its unit and its physical reading. The model reads $a(s)$ as the magnitude that an ideal accelerometer carried along the worldline would register at $s$; this ideal-instrument identification is adopted with the model in the same sense as the framework's ideal-clock reading of proper time and is not derived here. No accelerometer response law, calibration, frequency dependence, force law or interaction is specified or asserted; the definition asserts nothing about which bodies follow which worldlines; no measurement outcome and no statistical, uncertainty or empirical claim is made. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Definition with its well-definedness and its unit and congruence clauses justified by the cited suppliers. (a) A is continuous because x is C^2 (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline, def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration (b)); eta(A,A) is the sum of products of continuous component functions in any inertial chart (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart, thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions); eta(A,A) >= 0 pointwise by thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (b) together with the classification of nonzero spacelike vectors by def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors. Hence sqrt(eta(A,A)) is well defined for every tau as the nonnegative real whose square is eta(A,A) (def-rational-power). Units are read off directly from def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions, which lists the unit metre per second squared for the four-acceleration and the dimensionless matrix diag(-1,1,1,1) for eta in an inertial chart. (b) If U = c n along x with c a constant, then A = dU/dtau = c d(n o x)/dtau; the derivative of the field n along the worldline is the covariant derivative nabla_{dx/dtau} n = nabla_{cn} n = c nabla_n n = c a_cg by the defining properties of the flat covariant derivative along curves (def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space (d)); hence A = c^2 a_cg and eta(A,A) = c^4 eta(a_cg,a_cg), so a = c^2 sqrt(eta(a_cg,a_cg)) because c > 0. The acceleration a_cg is spacelike or zero by def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics (b), so eta(a_cg,a_cg) >= 0. (c) The scope clause records that the accelerometer reading is an ideal-instrument identification of the model and that no apparatus, force or measurement model is asserted; this mirrors the treatment of clock readings in post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and of wave frequencies in def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency. No choice principle is used.

items.physical_scope: Conditional kinematic definition inside the flat classical special-relativistic model: the proper acceleration of a C^2 future timelike worldline, its SI unit, and its identification with the magnitude of an ideal accelerometer reading. It presupposes ideal clocks and rods and the model's SI conventions; it asserts no force law, no accelerometer response or calibration model, no gravity, no rotational or quantum effect and no measurement, statistical or empirical content, and it makes no claim about any material body.

items.title: The uniformly accelerated worldline: hyperbolic motion, constant four-acceleration magnitude, and identification as a Rindler flow line
items.statement:
Let $c > 0$ and $\alpha > 0$, set $R := c^2/\alpha$, and let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski space with an inertial chart $\chi = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, $x^0 = c t$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]). Write $x^a(\tau):=\chi^a(x(\tau))$ for the coordinate components of the curve $x:\mathbb R\to A$ defined by $x(\tau) := \chi^{-1}(R \sinh \theta, R \cosh \theta, 0, 0)$, where $\theta := \alpha \tau/c$.

(a) **Regularity, causal character and parametrization.** $x$ is $C^\infty$, and $x'(\tau) = c(\cosh \theta, \sinh \theta, 0, 0)$ is future timelike for every $\tau$ ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]), so $x$ is a future timelike worldline ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]). Since $\eta(x',x') = -c^2$ is constant, the parameter $\tau$ is a proper-time parameter of the curve: the proper-time function $T$ of [[def-sr-proper-time]] satisfies $T(b)-T(a)=b-a$ for all $a < b$ in $\mathbb R$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]]), and the four-velocity is $U := dx/d\tau = c(\cosh \theta, \sinh \theta, 0, 0)$ with $\eta(U,U) = -c^2$ ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]], [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (a)).

(b) **Constant four-acceleration magnitude.** The four-acceleration $A := dU/d\tau = \alpha(\sinh \theta, \cosh \theta, 0, 0)$ satisfies $\eta(A,A) = \alpha^2$ and $\eta(U,A) = 0$. The chart coordinate velocity is $dx^1/dt = c \tanh \theta$, so $|dx^1/dt| < c$ for every $\tau$, and $x^1 = R \cosh \theta > R|\sinh \theta| = |x^0|$ for every $\tau$: the worldline lies in the right wedge $W := \{x^1 > |x^0|\}$ and its speed in the chart tends to $c$ only as $\tau \to \pm\infty$.

(c) **Rindler flow line.** Let $\Phi(\theta,\rho,y,z) := \chi^{-1}(\rho \sinh \theta, \rho \cosh \theta, y, z)$ on $\mathbb R \times (0,\infty) \times \mathbb R^2$ and let $n := \rho^{-1} \partial_\theta$ be the Rindler congruence of [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (b), whose pullback metric is $-\rho^2 d\theta^2 + d\rho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2$ and whose congruence acceleration $a_{\mathrm{cg}} := \nabla_n n$ is $\rho^{-1} \partial_\rho$, with $\eta(a_{\mathrm{cg}},a_{\mathrm{cg}}) = \rho^{-2}$ ([[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]], [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]]). Then $x$ is exactly the flow line $\Phi(\cdot, R, 0, 0)$ reparametrized by $\theta = \alpha \tau/c$, and along $x$ one has $A = c^2 a_{\mathrm{cg}}$: the four-acceleration of the worldline is $c^2$ times the congruence acceleration, and $\eta(a_{\mathrm{cg}},a_{\mathrm{cg}}) = 1/R^2 = \alpha^2/c^4$ on the flow line $\rho = R$.

(d) **Asymptotic behaviour.** Along $x$ one has $x^1 - x^0 = R e^{-\theta} \to 0$ with $x^0 \to +\infty$ as $\tau \to +\infty$, and $x^1 + x^0 = R e^{\theta} \to 0$ with $x^0 \to -\infty$ as $\tau \to -\infty$: the worldline approaches each of the null planes $\{x^1 = x^0\}$ and $\{x^1 = -x^0\}$ asymptotically without meeting either, and the chart coordinate speed tends to $c$ at both ends.

(e) **Scope.** This is an exact kinematic computation in the affine model. It uses no force law, no mass, no clock hypothesis and no empirical input; beyond identifying the displayed parameter with the proper time of the curve, only the flow parametrization of the congruence is used. The curve is not asserted to be a geodesic and no statement is made about the forces that would maintain it. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Exact computation with the hyperbolic identities and their derivatives. (a) Differentiating the two components of x with the chain rule (thm-chain-rule, def-derivative) and thm-hyperbolic-identities-and-derivatives gives x' = c(cosh theta, sinh theta, 0, 0); cosh > 0 makes it future and eta(x',x') = c^2(-cosh^2 + sinh^2) = -c^2 (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). The integrand of def-sr-proper-time is the constant c, so its integral over [a,b] is c(b-a) and tau(b) - tau(a) = b - a; the assertions about the four-velocity then follow from lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization (iv) and thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (a). (b) Differentiating U gives A = alpha(sinh theta, cosh theta, 0, 0); eta(A,A) = alpha^2(cosh^2 - sinh^2) = alpha^2 and eta(U,A) = c alpha(-cosh sinh + sinh cosh) = 0 (thm-hyperbolic-identities-and-derivatives); the chart velocity is dx^1/dt = (dx^1/dtau)/(dt/dtau) = c sinh/cosh = c tanh, and cosh > |sinh| gives the wedge and the speed bound. (c) Direct comparison: Phi(theta, R, 0, 0) = (R sinh theta, R cosh theta, 0, 0) = x(tau) with theta = alpha tau/c, and the congruence data are those of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b); the identity A = c^2 a_cg is proved directly on the flow line: since dx/dtau = c n there, d(n o x)/dtau = nabla_{dx/dtau} n = c nabla_n n = c a_cg by the defining properties of the flat covariant derivative along curves (def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space (d)), so A = dU/dtau = c d(n o x)/dtau = c^2 a_cg. (d) The identities x^1 -+ x^0 = R(cosh -+ sinh) = R e^{-+theta} and e^{+-theta} -> 0 (thm-exponential-limits-and-range) give the limits; tanh -> +-1 gives the speed statement. (e) Scope only. No choice principle is used: all steps are finite-dimensional algebra and calculus.

items.title: The material metric of a congruence: evolution of rest separations and preservation of the internal metric under Born rigidity
items.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a nonempty open subset of affine Minkowski space $A$, $c>0$, and let $n:\Omega\to V$ be a $C^1$ future unit timelike field, $\eta(n,n)=-1$. Define the following first-order quantities in any inertial chart:

$$h^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b,\qquad h_{ab}:=\eta_{ab}+n_an_b,\qquad a^b:=n^c\partial_cn^b,\qquad\theta_{ab}:=h_a{}^ch_b{}^d\partial_{(c}n_{d)},$$

where symmetrization means half the sum, $n_a:=\eta_{ab}n^b$, and $h(v,w):=h_{ab}v^aw^b$. Here $h$ is $C^1$ and $a,\theta$ are continuous. The rest projection $h(v):=v+\eta(n,v)n$ is as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (c). For $C^1$ fields and tensors define

$$(L_nh)_{ab}:=n^c\partial_ch_{ab}+h_{cb}\partial_an^c+h_{ac}\partial_bn^c.$$

For smooth data, define the ordinary Lie derivative by $(\mathcal L_nh)(X,Y):=n(h(X,Y))-h([n,X],Y)-h(X,[n,Y])$ for smooth vector fields $X,Y$; the brackets have the coordinate formula of [[prop-coordinate-formula-for-the-lie-bracket]]. These first-order coordinate formulas transform tensorially under affine inertial chart changes and agree, on smooth fields, with [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]], [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]] and the ordinary smooth Lie derivative. Say the $C^1$ field is **Born rigid** when $L_nh=0$; the identity $L_nh=2\theta$ makes this equivalent to $\theta=0$.

(a) Let $J$ be a nonempty open interval, $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ a nonempty open set, and $\Phi:J\times B\to\Omega$ an injective $C^2$ immersion with $\partial_s\Phi=n(\Phi)$. Put $e_I:=\partial_{\xi^I}\Phi$, $I=1,2,3$, and $G_{IJ}(s,\xi):=h(e_I,e_J)$ at $\Phi(s,\xi)$. Then $n,e_1,e_2,e_3$ are linearly independent, $G$ is symmetric positive definite at every point, and its entries are $C^1$. Thus for each $s$ it is a $C^1$ positive-definite material metric on $B$. If $n$ and $\Phi$ are smooth, $G$ is a smooth Riemannian metric, as in the original smooth branch.

(b) For all $I,J$,

$$\partial_sG_{IJ}=(L_nh)(e_I,e_J)=2\theta(e_I,e_J),\qquad\partial_\tau G_{IJ}=2c\theta(e_I,e_J),$$

where $\tau=s/c$ is the proper-time parameter along each flow line, whose four-velocity is $cn$. For a nonzero label direction $e_I$, put $\ell_I:=\sqrt{h(e_I,e_I)}>0$ and $u_I:=h(e_I)/\ell_I$. This $u_I$ is a horizontal unit rest vector, and

$$\partial_\tau\ell_I=c\theta(u_I,u_I)\ell_I.$$

The alternative normalized material vector $e_I/\ell_I$ need not be horizontal, but has the same $\theta$ contraction because $\theta$ is horizontal. Positive/negative expansion gives positive/negative fractional change of this material rest length per proper time.

(c) If $\theta=0$, then $\partial_sG_{IJ}=0$ and $G_{IJ}(s,\xi)$ is constant in $s$ for each fixed label, with no restriction on material-label separation: the entire internal metric is preserved exactly. Conversely, a nonzero contraction $\theta(e_I,e_J)$ gives a nonzero derivative of that metric component at the point and hence nonconstancy on a neighbourhood. The smooth Born-rigid branch and its original conclusions are included.

(d) This is a local statement about the given family and its material metric. Integrating the material metric at a common flow parameter gives an internal label-space length; it does not identify that length with a finite endpoint distance on a single observer's orthogonal simultaneity hyperplane without an additional argument. No matter model, elasticity, field equation, global rigidity theorem, boundary condition or choice principle is used.
items.strategy:
Use only first derivatives of $n$ and two derivatives of $\Phi$. The coordinate rules are tensorial under constant Lorentz changes of inertial coordinates by [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]; for smooth data they agree with the established smooth definitions. Differentiating $\eta(n,n)=-1$ gives $n_b\partial_an^b=0$, hence $\eta(n,a)=0$. Expansion of the projected symmetrization gives
$$2\theta_{ab}=\partial_an_b+\partial_bn_a+n_aa_b+a_an_b.$$
Differentiating $h_{ab}=\eta_{ab}+n_an_b$ in the displayed first-order Lie formula gives exactly this right side, proving $L_nh=2\theta$. The projectors make $\theta$ horizontal in both slots.
For the material fields, equality of the mixed partials of $C^2$ components of $\Phi$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]) and the total chain rule ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]) give
$$\partial_se_I^a=\partial_{\xi^I}n^a(\Phi)=(\partial_bn^a)(\Phi)e_I^b.$$
Differentiating $G_{IJ}=h_{ab}(\Phi)e_I^ae_J^b$ by the product rule gives the displayed coordinate formula for $(L_nh)(e_I,e_J)$, and thus $\partial_sG_{IJ}=2\theta(e_I,e_J)$. This direct calculation does not invoke a smooth-only Lie-bracket supplier for $C^1$ fields. In the smooth branch, the same mixed-partial identity is the usual commuting material-coordinate calculation $[n,e_I]=0$ ([[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], [[prop-coordinate-formula-for-the-lie-bracket]]), and recovers the original smooth route.
The derivative of $\Phi$ has four independent columns by immersion, so no nonzero linear combination of the three $e_I$ lies in $\operatorname{span}(n)$. The rest projection has that one-dimensional kernel and is positive definite on $n^\perp$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]](c)); hence $G$ is positive definite. $h(\Phi)$ and $e_I$ are $C^1$, so $G$ is $C^1$, and smooth if all data are smooth. Along a flow line $\partial_s\Phi=n$ is nonzero future timelike, and the proper-time definition gives $d\tau/ds=\sqrt{-\eta(n,n)}/c=1/c$, so $\partial_\tau=c\partial_s$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]). Apply the chain rule to $\ell_I^2=G_{II}$: $\partial_\tau\ell_I=c\theta(e_I,e_I)/\ell_I$. Since $h(e_I)-e_I$ is parallel to $n$, horizontality gives $\theta(e_I,e_I)=\ell_I^2\theta(u_I,u_I)$, proving the fractional-rate formula. If $\theta=0$, the interval zero-derivative corollary [[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]] proves constancy for each fixed label. A nonzero derivative prevents local constancy. All claims, including the smooth special case, are proved with the stated finite regularity and no zero tangent is called timelike.

items.title: The Rindler chart: causal horizons of a uniformly accelerated observer and the restrictions of radar time and distance
items.statement:
Adopt [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]], [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] and [[post-sr-causal-signal-propagation]], and the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] ($x^0 = c t$). Let $x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ be the chart of an inertial frame ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]) and let $W := \{x^1 > |x^0|\}$ be the right wedge. Let $\Phi$ and $n$ be the Rindler chart and congruence of [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (b): $\Phi(\theta,\rho,y,z) = (\rho \sinh \theta, \rho \cosh \theta, y, z)$ on $\mathbb R \times (0,\infty) \times \mathbb R^2$ with inverse $\rho = \sqrt{(x^1)^2 - (x^0)^2}$, $\theta = \frac12 \log((x^1+x^0)/(x^1-x^0))$, pullback metric $-\rho^2 d\theta^2 + d\rho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2$, and acceleration field $a_{\mathrm{cg}} = \nabla_n n = \rho^{-1} \partial_\rho$. Fix $\rho_0 > 0$ and real $y_0,z_0$, and let $O$ be the congruence worldline $\rho = \rho_0$, $y = y_0$, $z = z_0$, parametrized by its proper time $\tau$ with $\theta = c \tau/\rho_0$; by [[def-sr-proper-acceleration]] its proper acceleration is $c^2/\rho_0$. Write $U(q) := q^0 + q^1$ and $V(q) := q^0 - q^1$ for events $q$, so that $U = \rho e^{\theta}$ and $V = -\rho e^{-\theta}$ on $W$, and write $\le$ and $J^+$, $J^-$ for the causal reachability relations of [[def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space]]. Then, conditionally on the adopted model:

(i) **Chart domain and light rays.** $\Phi$ is a smooth bijection of $\mathbb R \times (0,\infty) \times \mathbb R^2$ onto $W$ with the stated smooth inverse, so the chart domain is exactly $W$ and $\rho = 0$ is not part of its coordinate domain. The boundary of $W$ in the affine model is $\{x^1 = |x^0|\}$, with arbitrary $x^2,x^3$: it is the union of the two null half-planes $\{x^1 = x^0 \ge 0\}$ and $\{x^1 = -x^0 \ge 0\}$. These half-planes are portions of the full null planes appearing as causal horizons in (ii); the full planes are not the wedge boundary. Along the worldline $\rho = \rho_0$ one has $V = -\rho_0 e^{-\theta} \to 0^-$ and $U \to +\infty$ as $\theta \to +\infty$, while $U = \rho_0 e^{\theta} \to 0^+$ and $V \to -\infty$ as $\theta \to -\infty$. The future null straight lines of the model that lie in the plane $y = y_0$, $z = z_0$ and meet $O$ are exactly the lines of constant $V$ (on which $d\theta = +d\rho/\rho$) and the lines of constant $U$ (on which $d\theta = -d\rho/\rho$).

(ii) **Causal horizons.** An event $q$ satisfies $q \le p$ for some event $p$ of $O$ if and only if $V(q) < 0$; an event $q$ satisfies $p \le q$ for some event $p$ of $O$ if and only if $U(q) > 0$. Consequently no event with $V(q) \ge 0$ can ever influence $O$; this set contains the null plane $\{x^1 = x^0\}$, the left wedge $\{x^1 < -|x^0|\}$ and the future wedge $\{x^0 > |x^1|\}$; and no event with $U(q) \le 0$ can ever be influenced by $O$, a set containing the null plane $\{x^1 = -x^0\}$, the left wedge and the past wedge $\{x^0 < -|x^1|\}$. The null plane $\{x^1 = x^0\}$ is the boundary of the causal past of $O$ (the future horizon: the surface its worldline approaches as $\theta \to +\infty$), and the null plane $\{x^1 = -x^0\}$ is the boundary of the causal future of $O$ (the past horizon); every event of the left wedge is causally unrelated to $O$ in both directions. The same criteria with $O$ any other congruence worldline $\rho = \rho_1$, $y = y_1$, $z = z_1$ hold verbatim: the constants $\rho_0$, $y_0$, $z_0$ do not enter.

(iii) **Radar time and distance to a coaxial congruence reflector.** Fix $\rho_m > 0$ with $\rho_m \ne \rho_0$ and let $R_m$ be the congruence worldline $\rho = \rho_m$, $y = y_0$, $z = z_0$ (a second uniformly accelerated observer, coaxial with $O$, with proper acceleration $c^2/\rho_m$). Let $e_-$ be the event of $O$ at parameter $\theta_e$ (so $\tau(e_-) = \rho_0 \theta_e/c$ up to the base point of $\tau$), let $q_m$ be the event of $R_m$ lying on the future null straight line from $e_-$ in the plane $y = y_0$, $z = z_0$, and let $e_+$ be the event of $O$ lying on the future null straight line from $q_m$; the reflection at $q_m$ is idealized as instantaneous and as leaving $R_m$'s motion unchanged, as in [[def-sr-operational-radar-protocol]]. Then $e_-, q_m, e_+$ exist uniquely, the Rindler time of $q_m$ is $\theta_m = \theta_e + |\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$, the return event satisfies $\theta(e_+) = \theta_e + 2|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$ and $(\theta_e + \theta(e_+))/2 = \theta_m$, so the round trip lasts $2|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$ in Rindler time and $(2\rho_0/c)|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$ in $O$'s proper time. The radar protocol therefore assigns to $q_m$ the radar time $\tau_{\mathrm{rad}}(q_m) = (\rho_0/c) \theta_m$ plus the base constant of $\tau$ and the radar distance $\rho_{\mathrm{rad}}(q_m) = \rho_0 |\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$; within this coaxial family the radar-time level sets are the intersections of the Rindler rest slices $\theta=\mathrm{const}$ with $y=y_0$, $z=z_0$, excluding the observer radius $\rho_0$ ([[def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance]]). The radar distance is not the rest distance: in the slice $\theta = \theta_m$ the two worldlines are at rest distance $|\rho_m - \rho_0|$, whereas for $\rho_m = 2\rho_0$ the radar distance is $\rho_0 \log 2 < \rho_0$, because $\log$ is strictly increasing and $e > 2$ implies $\log 2 < \log e = 1$ ([[cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]). For every distinct positive reflector radius the notions differ: with $r = \rho_m/\rho_0$, one has $\log r < r - 1$ when $r > 1$ and $-\log r > 1 - r$ when $0 < r < 1$. The two distance formulas agree only at $r = 1$, where both have the continuous degenerate value zero. The coincident case is not a nonzero emission-reflection-reception triple of the protocol, whose distinct-reflector hypothesis remains in force. As $\rho_m \to 0^+$ the round-trip proper time and the radar distance grow without bound while the reflector's proper acceleration $c^2/\rho_m$ diverges; as $\rho_m \to +\infty$ the round-trip proper time and the radar distance also grow without bound while the reflector's proper acceleration tends to $0$.

(iv) **Restrictions of the protocol.** No event with $V \ge 0$ --- in particular no event of the horizon plane $\{x^1 = x^0\}$, of the left wedge or of the future wedge --- can be assigned a radar time or radar distance by this protocol from $O$, because by (ii) it cannot causally precede any reception event on $O$: the required reflection-to-reception leg is impossible. Separately, every event with $U \le 0$ lacks an emission-to-reflection leg from $O$. Thus any event admitting this radar triple must satisfy $U > 0$ and $V < 0$, equivalently it must belong to $W$; the horizon is at infinite radar distance in the limit $\rho_m \to 0^+$. For example $q = x^{-1}(2\rho_0,0,y_0,z_0)$ has $U(q) = V(q) = 2\rho_0 > 0$. It is causally after $O$ at $\theta = 0$, since the displacement is $(2\rho_0,-\rho_0,0,0)$, future timelike, and it even lies on a future null ray from $O$ at $\theta = \log 2$, with displacement $(5\rho_0/4,-5\rho_0/4,0,0)$. Nevertheless it cannot send a causal return to $O$, so it receives no radar assignment from $O$. The protocol therefore does not extend to a global coordinate system of $A$.

(v) **Scope.** All clauses are conditional computations and readings in flat classical spacetime with ideal clocks, ideal light rays and ideal reflectors, for the specified congruence worldlines. They are not empirical claims and contain no measurement, apparatus, source, detector or statistical content; gravitation, media, dispersion, finite resolution, quantum effects and material models of the reflector are excluded. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Instantiate the causality lemmas of the causal model in the Rindler chart. (i) The chart assertions are those of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b), together with the identities U = rho e^{theta}, V = -rho e^{-theta}: on a line of constant V one has rho = rho_0 e^{theta - theta_0}, so dtheta = drho/rho and ds^2 = -rho^2 dtheta^2 + drho^2 = 0 exactly, and the tangent with increasing theta has positive time component, so the line is future null; on a line of constant U one has rho = rho_0 e^{theta_0 - theta} and dtheta = -drho/rho, and again ds^2 = 0 with a future tangent (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets, post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light). The limits along rho = rho_0 use the defining exponentials. The wedge boundary follows from the continuous inequality x1>|x0|: its closure is x1>=|x0|, since a boundary point is approached by increasing x1 by a positive amount. Thus the boundary is x1=|x0|, comprising only the indicated half-planes; at fixed finite theta, rho tending to zero does not parametrize the entire boundary. (ii) Write p(theta)=(rho_0 sinh theta,rho_0 cosh theta,y_0,z_0), Up=rho_0 e^theta, Vp=-rho_0 e^(-theta), and r^2=(q^2-y_0)^2+(q^3-z_0)^2. For a displacement D, the future causal coordinate criterion is equivalent to DeltaU>=0, DeltaV>=0 and DeltaU DeltaV>=r^2: D0=(DeltaU+DeltaV)/2, D1=(DeltaU-DeltaV)/2 and D0^2-D1^2=DeltaU DeltaV. For q<=p, necessity gives Vp-Vq>=0, hence Vq<=Vp<0. Conversely if Vq<0, as theta tends to +infinity the difference Vp-Vq tends to the positive number -Vq and Up-Uq tends to +infinity. Therefore both differences are positive and their product exceeds the fixed r^2 for sufficiently large theta; the coordinate criterion proves q<=p. For p<=q, necessity gives Uq-Up>=0, hence Uq>=Up>0. Conversely if Uq>0, as theta tends to -infinity the difference Uq-Up tends to the positive number Uq and Vq-Vp tends to +infinity; again their product eventually exceeds r^2 and p<=q follows. These complete arguments include arbitrary transverse positions. The full planes V=0 and U=0 are respectively the boundaries of these open causal unions; direct coordinate signs give the left/future/past wedge inclusions. The signal reading is conditional on post-sr-causal-signal-propagation, and the criteria do not depend on rho_0,y_0,z_0. (iii) The null line of constant V through e_- has rho = rho_0 e^{theta-theta_e}, which is increasing in theta; it meets rho = rho_m at theta_m = theta_e + log(rho_m/rho_0) when rho_m > rho_0. The null line of constant U through e_- has rho = rho_0 e^{theta_e-theta}, decreasing in theta; it meets rho = rho_m at theta_m = theta_e + log(rho_0/rho_m) when rho_m < rho_0. In both cases the displacement from e_- to q_m is a positive multiple of (1,1,0,0) or (1,-1,0,0), hence future null, and theta_m = theta_e + |log(rho_m/rho_0)|. From q_m the return line is the other null family: it reaches rho = rho_0 at theta(e_+) = theta_m + |log(rho_m/rho_0)| = theta_e + 2|log(rho_m/rho_0)|, again along a future null displacement, and uniqueness holds because through a point of the plane there passes exactly one future null line of each family and a fixed congruence worldline is met by such a line in exactly one event. The proper time of O between the two events is rho_0 (theta(e_+) - theta_e)/c by def-sr-proper-time and lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization applied to the unit-tangent flow line; def-sr-operational-radar-protocol converts the round trip into radar time (tau(e_-)+tau(e_+))/2 and radar distance c(tau(e_+)-tau(e_-))/2, giving the displayed values. The comparison with the rest distance uses the slice metric drho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b) and def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance; the numerical case rho_m = 2rho_0 uses log 2 < 1, which follows from e > 2, log e = 1 and strict increase of log (cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three, thm-natural-logarithm-laws). For the full equality classification, put $r=\rho_m/\rho_0>0$. By thm-logarithm-derivative-and-integral, log is differentiable on $(0,\infty)$ with derivative $1/u$, and therefore continuous there by cor-differentiable-implies-continuous. If $r>1$, cor-mean-value-theorem on $[1,r]$ gives $\xi\in(1,r)$ with $\log r=(r-1)/\xi<r-1$. If $0<r<1$, the same theorem on $[r,1]$ gives $\xi\in(r,1)$ with $-\log r=(1-r)/\xi>1-r$. Multiplying by $\rho_0>0$ proves radar distance strictly smaller than rest distance for an outer reflector and strictly larger for an inner reflector. Only $r=1$ gives zero in both formulas. Their continuity at $r=1$ follows from continuity of log and absolute value; this is the degenerate formula extension, not an assertion that a zero-length null leg satisfies the distinct-reflector protocol. The limits as rho_m -> 0^+ and rho_m -> +infinity follow from |log| -> +infinity and from c^2/rho_m. (iv) A radar triple requires e_-<=q and q<=e_+ with e_-,e_+ on O, indeed both displacements null in the protocol. By (ii), Vq>=0 makes q<=e_+ impossible, while Uq<=0 makes e_-<=q impossible. This is a return obstruction in the former case and an emission obstruction in the latter; both are needed for the round trip. The displayed q=(2rho_0,0,y_0,z_0) has future timelike displacement (2rho_0,-rho_0,0,0) from O(0), norm -3rho_0^2<0. O(log2) has coordinates (3rho_0/4,5rho_0/4,y_0,z_0), yielding the displayed future null displacement to q. Since Vq=2rho_0>0 no causal return to O exists. The infinite radar distance as rho_m decreases to zero is the logarithmic limit in (iii), not a spacetime singularity. (v) Scope only. No choice principle is used.

items.title: The guided-ring Sagnac delay: return times and receiver proper-time difference for counter-propagating guided signals on a rotating ring
items.statement:
Adopt [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] and [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] and the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] ($x^0 = c t$). Let $x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ be the chart of an inertial frame ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]). Fix $R > 0$, a real $\Omega$ with $|\Omega| R < c$, a real $x^3_0$ and a real $\phi_0$, and put $\gamma := (1 - \Omega^2 R^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. A rigidly rotating circular ring of radius $R$ and height $x^3_0$ about the $x^3$-axis, with angular velocity $\Omega$, has material worldlines

$$W_{\phi_0}(t) := x^{-1}(c t,\; R \cos(\phi_0 + \Omega t),\; R \sin(\phi_0 + \Omega t),\; x^3_0),\qquad t \in \mathbb R.$$

(i) **The ring worldline and the ring congruence.** $W_{\phi_0}$ is a $C^\infty$ future timelike worldline with unit observer

$$n = \gamma\,\bigl(1,\;-(\Omega R/c)\sin(\phi_0+\Omega t),\;(\Omega R/c)\cos(\phi_0+\Omega t),\;0\bigr) = (\gamma/c)\,\partial_t|_{\varphi},$$

$\eta(n,n) = -1$, and four-velocity $U = c n = \gamma\,\partial_t|_{\varphi}$, $\eta(U,U) = -c^2$, where $\varphi := \phi - \Omega t$ is the rotating angular label of the ring material points; it is an unparametrized flow line of the rigid-rotation congruence $n = \gamma(r)\,[\partial_0 + (\Omega/c)(-x^2\partial_1 + x^1\partial_2)]$ restricted to $r = R$, and its proper time $\tau$ and the chart time $t$ satisfy $d\tau = dt/\gamma$, so $\tau = t/\gamma + \tau_0$ for an arbitrary proper-time origin $\tau_0$ on this worldline ([[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (c), [[def-sr-proper-time]], [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]]).

(ii) **The guided-signal model.** Adopt, as an explicit model assumption of an ideal circular guide attached to the ring and of the signal and detector model below, and not as a consequence of the postulates: two ideal signals are emitted at the common emission event $W_{\phi_0}(0)$ into the guide, one in the positive angular direction and one in the negative angular direction (respectively co-rotating and counter-rotating for $\Omega > 0$, with these roles reversed for $\Omega < 0$), and in the inertial chart they follow the curves $C_+$ and $C_-$ given by $\phi_+(t) = \phi_0 + c t/R$ and $\phi_-(t) = \phi_0 - c t/R$ with radius $R$ and height $x^3_0$, i.e. each guided signal has chart angular rate $+c/R$ or $-c/R$ along the guide ('inertial tangential speed $c$ along the guide'); the detector is an ideal clock carried by the ring material point labelled $\varphi = \phi_0$. Each of $C_+$ and $C_-$ is a future null curve of the chart: its tangent has time component $c$ and spatial part of Euclidean length $c$, so the tangent has $\eta$-norm $0$ and positive time component ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]).

(iii) **Return times and differences.** The displayed guided curves have all-real mathematical extensions; emitted signals are their restrictions $t \ge 0$. On those extensions $C_+$ meets the worldline $W_{\phi_0}$ exactly at the chart times $2 \pi k R/(c - \Omega R)$, $k \in \mathbb Z$, and $C_-$ exactly at the chart times $2 \pi k R/(c + \Omega R)$, $k \in \mathbb Z$; the smallest positive meeting times are $t_1 := 2 \pi R/(c - \Omega R) > 0$ and $t_2 := 2 \pi R/(c + \Omega R) > 0$. Hence the two counter-propagating signals emitted at the same event reunite with the emitting material point at the reception events $W_{\phi_0}(t_1)$ and $W_{\phi_0}(t_2)$, each having gained exactly one circuit relative to that material point, and the chart-time difference of the two reunions is $t_1 - t_2 = 4 \pi \Omega R^2/(c^2 - \Omega^2 R^2) > 0$ for $\Omega > 0$. The proper-time difference measured by the detector ideal clock is $(t_1 - t_2)/\gamma = 4 \pi \Omega R^2/(c^2 \sqrt{1 - \Omega^2R^2/c^2})$. For $\Omega = 0$ (inertial ring) $t_1 = t_2 = 2 \pi R/c$ and both differences vanish; for $\Omega < 0$ the sign of the first difference reverses and the roles of $C_+$ and $C_-$ are interchanged.

(iv) **Relation to the ring rest-synchronization holonomy.** On the fixed-height timelike cylinder $C = \{r = R,\ x^3 = x^3_0\}$, material worldlines have constant rotating label. Its rest lines instead vary $\varphi$ on an angular lift and satisfy $dt/d\varphi = \Omega R^2/(c^2 - \Omega^2R^2)$, being integral curves of $\partial_\varphi + [\Omega R^2/(c^2 - \Omega^2R^2)]\,\partial_t$; for $\Omega = 0$ they are $t = \text{constant}$ circles; one circuit $\varphi \to \varphi + 2 \pi$ has the chart-time holonomy $\Delta t_h = 2 \pi \Omega R^2/(c^2 - \Omega^2R^2) = (t_1 - t_2)/2$ and the receiver proper-time holonomy $\Delta \tau_h = \Delta t_h/\gamma = 2 \pi \Omega R^2/(c^2 \sqrt{1 - \Omega^2R^2/c^2}) = (1/2)(t_1 - t_2)/\gamma$, exactly half of the detector proper-time difference of (iii); for $\Omega = 0$ both holonomies vanish. The ambient three-dimensional rest distribution of the rotating congruence is nowhere integrable for $\Omega \neq 0$, so no ambient rest-simultaneity hypersurface exists, while the one-dimensional rest distribution restricted to the fixed-height cylinder $C$ is locally integrable and has the global holonomy just computed, nonvanishing exactly when $\Omega \neq 0$; the return-time computation of (iii) uses only the guided null curves and the material worldline and does not use either integrability property ([[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (c), [[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]]).

(v) **Scope.** All quantities are conditional model computations for the specified ring, guide, signal and detector idealizations. The guided-signal curves are an adopted device model: the ideal vacuum light rays of [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] are straight future null lines and do not circulate around the ring by themselves, and no assertion is made about optical fibers, refractive media, dispersion, absorption, finite resolution, apparatus calibration, interference phase or wave optics, or about one-way synchronization conventions between distinct ring observers; no measurement outcome, statistical inference or empirical claim is made, the values of $R$ and $\Omega$ are parameters and not measured quantities, and no choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Direct computation on the fixed-height timelike cylinder C={r=R,x^3=x^3_0}. (i) Differentiate W with the sine/cosine derivative and chain-rule suppliers to obtain dot W=(c,-Omega R sin phi,Omega R cos phi,0), where phi=phi_0+Omega t. Pythagoras gives eta(dot W,dot W)=-c^2+Omega^2R^2=-c^2/gamma^2<0 and dot W^0=c>0. The exact proper-time and four-velocity suppliers give d tau=dt/gamma, n=(gamma/c)dot W with eta(n,n)=-1, and U=gamma dot W=cn with eta(U,U)=-c^2. Since dot W=partial_t|varphi, n=(gamma/c)partial_t|varphi and U=gamma partial_t|varphi. Parametrization by s=c tau makes the material curve an integral curve of n; chart-time parametrization gives the same unparametrized flow line. (ii) Differentiating the adopted C_+ and C_- curves gives time component c and spatial norm c, hence future null tangents, without deducing the circular guide model from straight vacuum-ray postulates. (iii) The exact trigonometric addition/parity, quarter-turn, and zero-set suppliers show that two sine/cosine pairs agree exactly when their angles differ by 2 pi k: addition gives sin(angle difference)=0 and cos(angle difference)=1; the zero-set result puts the difference in pi Z, and pi shifts negate cosine, leaving only even integers. Thus C_+ meets the material curve when (c/R-Omega)t=2 pi k, while C_- meets it when -(c/R+Omega)t=2 pi k. In the latter relabel m=-k. Both denominators c-Omega R and c+Omega R are positive on |Omega|R<c, so all-real extensions have exactly the stated integer meeting sets, and signals emitted at t=0 have first positive reunion at winding magnitude one. Subtract the two return times to obtain Delta t=4 pi Omega R^2/(c^2-Omega^2R^2), then divide by gamma to obtain the detector proper-time difference. Omega=0 gives equal returns and zero differences; negative Omega interchanges co-/counter-rotation and reverses the signed differences. (iv) The rigid-rotation supplier gives the fixed-height cylinder metric -D dt^2+2 Omega R^2 dt dvarphi+R^2 dvarphi^2, D=c^2-Omega^2R^2>0. Orthogonality to the material tangent partial_t gives -D dt+Omega R^2 dvarphi=0, so rest lines are generated by partial_varphi+(Omega R^2/D)partial_t, not by constant-label material lines. Integration over a positive 2 pi angular lift gives Delta t_h=2 pi Omega R^2/D and the signed receiver offset Delta tau_h=Delta t_h/gamma, exactly half the corresponding signal-return differences. At zero Omega the rest lines close at constant t. The ambient rank-three rest distribution is locally nonintegrable for nonzero Omega by the rigid-rotation/Frobenius suppliers; the cylinder's rank-one rest lines are locally integrable and their nonzero winding offset is a separate global obstruction. (v) All device-model, ideal-clock, no-measurement and empirical-scope qualifications are retained. No choice principle is used.

B. Crowell, Special Relativity, revision 2020-12-10 (author-published undergraduate textbook, 246 PDF pages): Sections 8.1.1-8.1.3 pp. 165-166 (no Einstein synchronization in a rotating frame, the synchronization discrepancy accumulating around a closed circuit, and the Sagnac effect of a rotating ring, with the time shift 2 A omega/c^2 and the ring-laser and fiber-gyroscope examples); signature (+---) converted to (-+++), c = 1 formulas restored to x^0 = c t

items.physical_scope: Conditional kinematic computation in flat classical special relativity for an ideal rigidly rotating circular ring, an adopted ideal circular guide carrying two counter-propagating guided signals with inertial tangential speed c, and an ideal clock detector on the ring. The guide and detector models are explicit idealizations, not consequences of the special-relativistic postulates; the item excludes real optical fibers, refractive and dispersive media, apparatus, finite resolution, interference and wave optics, gravitation and quantum effects, and it makes no measurement, statistical or empirical claim and no claim about sending signals between different material points of the ring.

items.title: Bell's rockets and thread: constant chart separation and the criterion for longitudinal expansion of the translated congruence
items.statement:
Adopt [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] and the SI conventions $x^0=ct$ of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] in an inertial chart ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]). Let $J$ be an open interval containing $0$, let $q:J\to\mathbb R$ be $C^2$ with $|q'(t)|<c$, set $\beta=q'/c$ and $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, let $L>0$, and fix transverse coordinates $(y_0,z_0)$. The rocket and thread-element worldlines are $x_\xi(t)=x^{-1}(ct,q(t)+\xi,y_0,z_0)$, with labels in an open interval $I$ containing $[0,L]$; the rockets are labels $0,L$.

(a) Every member is $C^2$ future timelike: its chart-time tangent is $(c,q',0,0)$ with squared norm $-c^2/\gamma^2<0$. Its common proper-time function is $\tau(t):=\int_0^t\gamma(v)^{-1}dv$, and its proper four-velocity is $U=\gamma(c,q',0,0)$ with squared norm $-c^2$. All members have equal chart velocity and acceleration, $q',q''$, and their chart separation is the constant $L$.

(b) The four-dimensional extension is essential for applying the material-family lemma. Choose open transverse intervals $Y,Z$ containing $y_0,z_0$, put $\sigma:=c\tau$, let $t=t(\sigma)$ be the inverse on $c\tau(J)$, and set

$$\Phi(\sigma,\xi,y,z):=x^{-1}(ct(\sigma),q(t(\sigma))+\xi,y,z),\qquad(\xi,y,z)\in B:=I\times Y\times Z.$$

This is an injective $C^2$ immersion onto an open set, with $dt/d\sigma=\gamma/c$ and $\partial_\sigma\Phi=n(\Phi)$, where $n=\gamma(1,\beta,0,0)$ is a $C^1$ future unit field. Apply the first-order definitions in [[lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching]], which agree with [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] when smooth. The longitudinal unit rest vector is $s_\parallel:=\gamma(\beta,1,0,0)$, and

$$\theta(s_\parallel,s_\parallel)=\gamma^3q'q''/c^3.$$

This agrees with [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (d), is nonzero exactly where $q'q''\ne0$, and changes sign with that product. When $q$ is smooth the full original smooth-congruence branch is recovered. Restricting the extension to fixed $y_0,z_0$ gives the prescribed thread.

(c) For its material label tangent $e=\partial_\xi\Phi=(0,1,0,0)$, $h(e,e)=\gamma^2$ and $h(e)/\gamma=s_\parallel$. The vector $e/\gamma$ generally is not $s_\parallel$, but horizontality implies $\theta(e/\gamma,e/\gamma)=\theta(s_\parallel,s_\parallel)$. The internal longitudinal material metric is $G_{11}=\gamma^2$, so its length at common flow parameter is

$$\mathcal L(t):=\int_0^L\sqrt{G_{11}}\,d\xi=\gamma(t)L.$$

It is an internal material metric length, not automatically the finite endpoint distance on one observer's orthogonal simultaneity hyperplane. The local evolution is

$$\frac{d}{d\tau}\log(\mathcal L/L)=c\theta(s_\parallel,s_\parallel)=\gamma^3q'q''/c^2,\qquad\frac{d\mathcal L}{d\tau}=\gamma^4Lq'q''/c^2.$$

At a time with $q'=v$, $\mathcal L=L/\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}\ge L$, with equality exactly for $v=0$. Chart separation stays $L$; the material length is constant precisely when $q'{}^2$ is constant, and has nonzero local rate wherever $q'q''\ne0$.

(d) Under the stipulated material reading that thread elements follow these flow lines, the initial internal length is $\gamma(0)L$ and its relative factor is $\gamma(t)/\gamma(0)$. Relative to that initial state it stretches where $\gamma(t)>\gamma(0)$, shrinks where $\gamma(t)<\gamma(0)$, and has equal length where the factors agree. In the special initially resting case $q'(0)=0$, the initial length is $L$ and every state with $q'(t)\ne0$ has stretch factor $\gamma(t)>1$. No elasticity or failure criterion is supplied, so neither breaking nor a definite tension of an actual thread follows.

(e) The Rindler congruence in [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (b) is Born rigid, with constant internal rest separations and unequal proper accelerations $c^2/\rho$ at distinct radial labels ([[def-sr-proper-acceleration]]). Equal chart-velocity and acceleration profiles in the translated family do not imply Born rigidity where $q'q''\ne0$. Constant chart separation and constant internal rest metric are distinct kinematic conditions.

(f) This is a conditional flat-spacetime deduction for prescribed worldlines and the stated material reading. It assumes no dynamical or elastic model, force law, material failure criterion, measurement or empirical fact, and asserts nothing about real threads or rockets. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy:
(a) Differentiate the given worldlines. The chart-time tangent has norm $-c^2+q\prime{}^2=-c^2/\gamma^2$ and positive time component, so it is nonzero future timelike. Proper time gives $d\tau/dt=1/\gamma$ and $U=dx/d\tau=\gamma(c,q\prime,0,0)$; its norm is $-c^2$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]], [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]). The separation and equality of chart derivatives follow directly.
(b) Since $q$ is $C^2$, $\gamma$ is $C^1$ and $\tau\prime=1/\gamma$ is positive $C^1$, so $\tau$ is $C^2$ and strictly increasing. [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]] gives its $C^1$ inverse; its derivative $dt/d\tau=\gamma(t(\tau))$ is $C^1$, hence the inverse is $C^2$. Scaling to $\sigma=c\tau$ gives $dt/d\sigma=\gamma/c$. Thus $\Phi$ is $C^2$, its four derivative columns are $n,e_1,e_2,e_3$, and its determinant in the chart is $\gamma>0$. Its inverse is explicit from $t=x^0/c$, $\xi=x^1-q(t)$, $y=x^2,z=x^3$, so it is injective with open image and satisfies the precise $J\times B\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$ family hypothesis of [[lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching]]. The $C^1$ field $n$ depends only on $t=x^0/c$. Using the first-order projected formula for $\theta$, and the fact that $s_\parallel$ is horizontal, Writing $\dot\beta=d\beta/dt$, the only nonzero coordinate derivatives are $\partial_0n_0=-\gamma^3\beta\dot\beta/c$ and $\partial_0n_1=\gamma^3\dot\beta/c$. Therefore $s_\parallel^a s_\parallel^b\partial_an_b=\gamma^3\beta\dot\beta/c$, giving $\theta(s_\parallel,s_\parallel)=s_\parallel^a s_\parallel^b\partial_an_b=\gamma^3q\prime q\prime\prime/c^3$. This proves the formula with exactly $C^2$ data and agrees with [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]](d); it does not require a smooth-only supplier for the nonsmooth branch.
(c) Compute $h(e,e)=1+\gamma^2\beta^2=\gamma^2$ and $h(e)=e+\gamma\beta n=\gamma s_\parallel$. Since $\theta(n,\cdot)=0$, the difference of $e/\gamma$ and $s_\parallel$ is annihilated by $\theta$. Applying [[lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching]] to the four-dimensional family, then restricting to fixed transverse labels, gives $G=\operatorname{diag}(\gamma^2,1,1)$ and the length/rate identities. Independently $d\gamma/dt=\gamma^3q\prime q\prime\prime/c^2$ and $d/d\tau=\gamma d/dt$ give $d(\gamma L)/d\tau=\gamma^4Lq\prime q\prime\prime/c^2$. The derivative with respect to geometric proper length is instead $d/d\sigma=(\gamma/c)d/dt$. The length $\gamma L$ is exactly the integral of the pulled-back local rest metric over the fixed-label segment; the fixed-$\sigma$ segment need not lie in an endpoint observer's orthogonal hyperplane. The equality/constancy statements follow from $\gamma=(1-q\prime{}^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$.
(d) Compare $\mathcal L(t)$ with $\mathcal L(0)=\gamma(0)L$. This gives the factor and the stretch/shrink cases without an initial-rest hypothesis. Specializing $q\prime(0)=0$ gives the original initially resting stretch conclusion. Material failure and constitutive stress require an additional model and are not deduced.
(e) Apply the exact smooth Rindler clause of [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] and [[def-sr-proper-acceleration]]; its rigidity and unequal radial accelerations provide the stated contrast. (f) Retain all physical qualifications and the absence of empirical or material-dynamics conclusions.

items.title: Rindler radar distances worked: reflectors at twice and at half the observer's radius
items.statement:
Worked computation in the Rindler chart of [[pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar]]. Let $c > 0$, fix $\rho_0 > 0$ and take $y_0 = z_0 = 0$; let $O$ be the congruence worldline $\rho = \rho_0$ with Rindler time $\theta = c \tau/\rho_0$, and take the emission event $e_-$ at $\theta_e = 0$, so that $e_- = x^{-1}(0, \rho_0, 0, 0)$ in the inertial chart $x$.

(a) **Reflector at $\rho_m = 2\rho_0$.** The future null line from $e_-$ of constant $V$ has $V = -\rho_0$, and it meets $\rho = 2\rho_0$ at the Rindler time $\theta_m = \log 2$; using $\sinh(\log 2) = 3/4$ and $\cosh(\log 2) = 5/4$ ([[thm-hyperbolic-identities-and-derivatives]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]) the reflection event is $q_m = x^{-1}(3\rho_0/2, 5\rho_0/2, 0, 0)$, and the return event is $e_+ = x^{-1}(\rho_0 \sinh(2\log 2), \rho_0 \cosh(2\log 2), 0, 0) = x^{-1}(15\rho_0/8, 17\rho_0/8, 0, 0)$ at Rindler time $\theta(e_+) = 2 \log 2$. Thus $(\theta_e + \theta(e_+))/2 = \log 2 = \theta_m$, the radar time assigned to $q_m$ is $(\rho_0/c) \log 2$ plus the base constant of $O$'s proper time, and the radar distance is $\rho_0 \log 2$. The two worldlines $\rho = \rho_0$ and $\rho = 2\rho_0$ are at rest distance $\rho_0$ in the slice $\theta = \log 2$; since $e > 2$ gives $\log 2 < 1$ ([[cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]), the radar distance is strictly smaller than the rest distance.

(b) **Reflector at $\rho_m = \rho_0/2$.** The future null line from $e_-$ of constant $U$ has $U = \rho_0$, and it meets $\rho = \rho_0/2$ at the Rindler time $\theta_m = \log 2$; using $\sinh(\log 2) = 3/4$ and $\cosh(\log 2) = 5/4$ the reflection event is $q'_m = x^{-1}(3\rho_0/8, 5\rho_0/8, 0, 0)$ and the return event is again $e_+ = x^{-1}(15\rho_0/8, 17\rho_0/8, 0, 0)$ at Rindler time $2 \log 2$. The radar time is again $(\rho_0/c) \log 2$ plus the base constant and the radar distance is again $\rho_0 \log 2$, while the rest distance in the slice $\theta = \log 2$ is now $\rho_0/2$; since $e < 3 < 4$ gives $\log 2 > 1/2$ ([[cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]), the radar distance is now strictly larger than the rest distance.

(c) The two cases (a)-(b) give the same radar distance $\rho_0\log2$ at distinct rest distances $\rho_0$ and $\rho_0/2$; this demonstrates noninjectivity of the assignment as the reflector radius varies. To prove that radar distance is not determined by the rest distance alone, also take $\rho_m=3\rho_0/2$. With the same emission at $\theta_e=0$, the reflection occurs at $\theta_m=\log(3/2)$, at $q''_m=x^{-1}(5\rho_0/8,13\rho_0/8,0,0)$, and the return occurs at $2\log(3/2)$, at $e''_+=x^{-1}(65\rho_0/72,97\rho_0/72,0,0)$. This reflector has rest distance $\rho_0/2$, equal to case (b), but radar distance $\rho_0\log(3/2)<\rho_0\log2$, because $3/2<2$ and $\log$ is strictly increasing. These equal inputs and unequal outputs prove the stated failure of dependence on rest distance alone. The original two cases both satisfy $\theta_m=(\theta_e+\theta(e_+))/2$ and have round-trip proper time $2\rho_0\log2/c$; the third case satisfies the same midpoint identity and has round-trip proper time $2\rho_0\log(3/2)/c$.

(d) **Scope.** Conditional model computation with ideal clocks, ideal light rays and ideal reflectors in the flat classical model; no measurement, apparatus, source or statistical claim, and no empirical inference, is made, and the idealizations of [[pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar]] (v) are retained.
items.strategy: Substitute the two reflector radii into the exact radar computation of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (iii). (a) With theta_e = 0 the constant-V line through e_- carries V = -rho_0; meeting rho = 2rho_0 gives -2rho_0 e^{-theta} = -rho_0, i.e. e^{-theta} = 1/2 and theta_m = log 2; the chart coordinates of q_m are (2rho_0 sinh(log 2), 2rho_0 cosh(log 2), 0, 0) = (3rho_0/2, 5rho_0/2, 0, 0) by the exact values sinh(log 2) = 3/4, cosh(log 2) = 5/4, which follow from the defining exponentials. The return line is the constant-U line through q_m and meets rho = rho_0 at theta(e_+) = 2log 2, giving e_+ = (rho_0 sinh(2log 2), rho_0 cosh(2log 2), 0, 0) = (15rho_0/8, 17rho_0/8, 0, 0) (sinh(2log 2) = 15/8, cosh(2log 2) = 17/8). The radar time and distance follow from the protocol formula of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (iii) with the round-trip proper time rho_0(2log 2)/c of O; the rest distance uses the slice metric drho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 (def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance). The inequality log 2 < 1 is the strict increase of log and 2 < e (cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three, thm-natural-logarithm-laws). (b) With theta_e = 0 the constant-U line through e_- carries U = rho_0; meeting rho = rho_0/2 gives (rho_0/2) e^{theta} = rho_0, i.e. theta_m = log 2, and the reflection event is ((rho_0/2) sinh(log 2), (rho_0/2) cosh(log 2), 0, 0) = (3rho_0/8, 5rho_0/8, 0, 0); the return line is the constant-V line through q'_m and meets rho = rho_0 again at theta = 2log 2, giving the same return event as in (a). The radar quantities are as displayed, and log 2 > 1/2 follows from log4=2log2>log e=1, since 4 > e and log is strictly increasing (cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three, thm-natural-logarithm-laws). (c) Cases (a)-(b) alone prove that distinct reflector radii and rest distances can give the same radar distance; they do not establish failure of dependence on rest distance alone. For the additional radius 3rho_0/2, constant V=-rho_0 gives theta_m=log(3/2). The defining exponentials give sinh(log(3/2))=5/12 and cosh(log(3/2))=13/12; multiplying by 3rho_0/2 gives (5rho_0/8,13rho_0/8). The return has theta=2log(3/2), for which e^theta=9/4 and e^(-theta)=4/9, hence sinh theta=65/72 and cosh theta=97/72; multiplying by rho_0 gives the stated return coordinates. The outgoing displacement from (0,rho_0) is (5rho_0/8,5rho_0/8), future null. The return displacement from q''_m is (5rho_0/18,-5rho_0/18), future null. The third reflector and the radius rho_0/2 reflector both have rest distance rho_0/2, while their radar distances are rho_0 log(3/2) and rho_0 log2, unequal by strict increase of log. This completes the full claim with all earlier examples and midpoint calculations preserved. (d) Scope only. No choice principle is used.

items.title: The Rindler causal horizon is not a boundary or singularity of spacetime
items.statement:
In the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space with the inertial chart $x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, the null plane $H := \{x^1 = x^0\}$ is a boundary of the model in the following three senses: (i) no future causal curve crosses from $\{x^1 > x^0\}$ to $\{x^1 < x^0\}$; (ii) $H$ separates all causal relations, so no event of $\{x^1 > x^0\}$ is causally related to any event of $\{x^1 < x^0\}$; and (iii) the metric degenerates on $H$, so that $H$ is a singular boundary of the spacetime on which the model fails.

Here $H$ is the full causal-past boundary of the accelerated congruence; only its half-plane $\{x^1 = x^0 \ge 0\}$ belongs to the boundary of the right wedge $W = \{x^1 > |x^0|\}$.
items.strategy: Explicit witnesses checked against the coordinate criterion of lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion. (a) The affine segment y has constant derivative with coordinates (4,1,0,0); eta applied to it is -16+1=-15 < 0 and its time component is positive, so y is a future timelike curve by the definition of causal classification and the future cone; the coordinate function x^0 - x^1 along y is affine with values -1 and 2 at the endpoints, so it vanishes inside [0,1] and the crossing event y(1/3)=x^{-1}(1/3,1/3,0,0) lies on H. This is a direct refutation of the first two clauses of the quoted statement. (b) The displayed displacements (1,0,0,0) and (1,1/2,0,0) are future timelike, with norms -1 and -3/4 respectively by the coordinate criterion ((c) of the cited lemma), and the initial and final events straddle H while the middle event lies on it; r=(0,1,0,0) is explicitly off H. (c) Nondegeneracy and constancy of the metric matrix are read from the inertial chart (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart, def-sr-affine-minkowski-model); the domain property of Phi is clause (b) of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples. The crossing event is at y(1/3), not the falsely identified midpoint. The inertial metric is nondegenerate at every event; restricting a coordinate chart to the wedge changes neither it nor the model domain. Distinguish the two half-plane portions of the wedge boundary from the full horizon planes, as in the repaired Rindler theorem. (d) The worldline z is affine with constant future timelike tangent (c,0,0,0), so it is a future timelike worldline defined for all t (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline), and the sign of x^0 - x^1 = c t changes at t = 0. (e) Scope only. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Rindler radar distance between two coaxial observers is not symmetric under interchange
items.statement: Statement refuted: 'For every pair of future timelike worldlines y and y' of the model for which the radar protocol of def-sr-operational-radar-protocol applies with y as observer and y' as reflector, the radar distance assigned by y to the reflection event on y' equals the radar distance assigned by y' to the reflection event on y; that is, the radar distance between two observers is symmetric under interchange of observer and reflector.' Counterexample in the Rindler chart of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar with y = O the worldline rho = rho_0 and y' = R the worldline rho = 2rho_0 (coaxial, with the same y = z = 0 coordinates), rho_0 > 0, c > 0. (a) Radar distance from O to R. Emit from O at the Rindler time theta_e = 0, i.e. from e_- = x^{-1}(0, rho_0, 0, 0). By pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (iii) the reflection event on R is q_m = x^{-1}(3rho_0/2, 5rho_0/2, 0, 0) at Rindler time log 2 and the reception event on O is e_+ = x^{-1}(15rho_0/8, 17rho_0/8, 0, 0) at Rindler time 2 log 2; the round trip takes 2rho_0 log 2/c of O's proper time, so the radar distance assigned by O is D_1 := rho_0 log 2. (b) Radar distance from R to O. Emit from R at theta = 0, i.e. from r_- = x^{-1}(0, 2rho_0, 0, 0). The future null line from r_- towards O is the constant-U line with U = 2rho_0; it meets rho = rho_0 at the Rindler time log 2, at the reflection event q'_m = x^{-1}(3rho_0/4, 5rho_0/4, 0, 0), and the return line reaches R at the Rindler time 2 log 2, at the event x^{-1}(15rho_0/4, 17rho_0/4, 0, 0). The round trip takes 4rho_0 log 2/c of R's proper time, so the radar distance assigned by R is D_2 := 2rho_0 log 2. (c) Hence D_2/D_1 = 2 = rho_m/rho_0: the two radar distances between the same pair of worldlines differ, and the assignment is not symmetric. Both assignments are finite and both reflection events lie in the causal future of their respective emission events; the asymmetry is a property of the radar assignment with the two different observers, not a physical anisotropy. (d) Scope. Conditional model computation with ideal clocks, ideal light rays and ideal reflectors; the symmetric half-split convention of def-sr-operational-radar-protocol is retained, and no measurement, statistical or empirical claim is made.
items.strategy: Recompute the radar protocol of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (iii) with the roles of the two worldlines interchanged. (a) Recompute directly from the theorem and chart: from (0,rho_0), the constant-V=-rho_0 ray meets rho=2rho_0 at theta=log2, giving q_m=(3rho_0/2,5rho_0/2); its constant-U return meets rho=rho_0 at theta=2log2, giving (15rho_0/8,17rho_0/8). Both displacements are future null. This uses no B-page example as a supplier. (b) The future null line from r_- towards smaller rho is the constant-U line U = 2rho_0, i.e. rho = 2rho_0 e^{-theta}; it meets rho = rho_0 at theta = log 2, and the chart coordinates there are (rho_0 sinh(log 2), rho_0 cosh(log 2), 0, 0) = (3rho_0/4, 5rho_0/4, 0, 0) by sinh(log 2) = 3/4 and cosh(log 2) = 5/4 (thm-hyperbolic-identities-and-derivatives, thm-natural-logarithm-laws). The return line is the constant-V line through q'_m and meets rho = 2rho_0 at theta = 2log 2, with coordinates (2rho_0 sinh(2log 2), 2rho_0 cosh(2log 2), 0, 0) = (15rho_0/4, 17rho_0/4, 0, 0). The proper-time conversion factor on the worldline rho = const is rho/c per unit Rindler time by the proper-time formula in pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (iii), giving the round-trip proper times 2rho_0 log 2/c and 4rho_0 log 2/c respectively and the radar distances D_1 = rho_0 log 2 and D_2 = 2rho_0 log 2. (c) Since log2>log1=0, D1>0 and the quotient D_2/D_1=2 is well defined. The radius-dependent proper-time conversion factor, not any physical anisotropy, causes the two observer assignments to differ. (d) Scope only. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Guided-ring Sagnac delay worked at angular velocity Omega R = 3c/5
items.statement: Worked instance of pthm-sr-guided-ring-sagnac-delay. Let R > 0 and Omega = 3c/(5R), so that Omega R = 3c/5, |Omega|R < c and gamma = (1 - 9/25)^{-1/2} = 5/4. Work in the inertial chart with x^0 = c t and let the ring have its plane x^3 = 0 and let the emission event be E = x^{-1}(0, R, 0, 0), where the material point labelled varphi = 0 has phi_0 = 0. (a) Return times. The co-rotating guided signal has phi_+(t) = c t/R and the emitting material point has phi(t) = Omega t = 3c t/(5R); the signal meets that point when c t/R = 3c t/(5R) + 2 pi, i.e. t_1 = 5 pi R/c (the co-rotating relative angular rate is 2c/(5R)); the counter-rotating signal C_-, phi_-(t) = -c t/R, meets it when -c t/R = 3c t/(5R) - 2 pi, i.e. t_2 = 5 pi R/(4c), with signed relative angular rate -8c/(5R) and magnitude 8c/(5R). The reception events are e_1 = x^{-1}(5 pi R, R cos(3 pi), R sin(3 pi), 0) = x^{-1}(5 pi R, -R, 0, 0) and e_2 = x^{-1}(5 pi R/4, R cos(3 pi/4), R sin(3 pi/4), 0) = x^{-1}(5 pi R/4, -R/sqrt(2), R/sqrt(2), 0), where the angle values use the parity, addition and Pythagorean identities for sine and cosine (def-pi-via-first-positive-cosine-zero, thm-sine-and-cosine-addition-formulas, cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity). (b) Differences and the factor-2 holonomy check. The chart-time difference of the two reunions is t_1 - t_2 = 5 pi R/c - 5 pi R/(4c) = 15 pi R/(4c) = 4 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2R^2), and the detector proper-time difference is (t_1-t_2)·(4/5) = 3 pi R/c = 4 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 sqrt(1 - Omega^2R^2/c^2)). The ring rest-line chart-time holonomy of pthm-sr-guided-ring-sagnac-delay (iv) is Delta t_h = 15 pi R/(8c), exactly half of t_1 - t_2, and the corresponding receiver proper-time holonomy is (4/5)·15 pi R/(8c) = 3 pi R/(2c), exactly half of 3 pi R/c; this verifies the factor-2 relation of that clause. The ambient rest distribution of the rotating congruence is nowhere integrable while the fixed-height-cylinder-restricted one-dimensional rest distribution is locally integrable with the nonzero global holonomy 15 pi R/(8c) (thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (c)). (c) Inertial limit. For Omega = 0 with the same R the two return times are both 2 pi R/c and both differences vanish. (d) Scope. Conditional model computation with the adopted ideal circular guide, ideal signals and the ideal clock detector of pthm-sr-guided-ring-sagnac-delay (ii); no interference phase, apparatus, medium, measurement, statistical or empirical claim is made, and the idealizations of that theorem are retained.
items.strategy: Substitute Omega = 3c/(5R) into the exact formulas of pthm-sr-guided-ring-sagnac-delay. (a) The angle of the material point is phi(t) = Omega t = 3c t/(5R); the co-rotating guided signal has angle c t/R, so the relative angular rate is 2c/(5R) and the reunion condition is c t/R = 3c t/(5R) + 2 pi k, with smallest positive solution k = 1, i.e. t_1 = 2 pi R/(c - 3c/5) = 5 pi R/c; the counter-rotating signal has angle -c t/R, so the signed relative angular rate is -8c/(5R) and the condition is -c t/R = 3c t/(5R) - 2 pi k, i.e. t_2 = 2 pi R/(c + 3c/5) = 5 pi R/(4c). The reception events are obtained by substituting these times into the parametrisation of pthm-sr-guided-ring-sagnac-delay (i), with the elementary sine and cosine values cos(3 pi) = -1, sin(3 pi) = 0 and cos(3 pi/4) = -sin(3 pi/4) = -1/sqrt(2) supplied by the parity, addition, quarter-turn, positive-sine and Pythagorean identities: sin(pi/4)=cos(pi/4)>0 by the half-pi shift and positive-sine result, and each equals 1/sqrt(2) by Pythagoras; subsequent shifts give the displayed values. (b) The differences are the substitutions into 4 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2R^2) = 4 pi (3c/(5R))R^2/(c^2(1-9/25)) = 15 pi R/(4c) and into (t_1-t_2)/gamma with 1/gamma = 4/5; the holonomy Delta t_h = 2 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2R^2) evaluates to 2 pi (3c/(5R))R^2/(c^2(16/25)) = 15 pi R/(8c), half of 15 pi R/(4c), and its proper-time counterpart is (4/5)·15 pi R/(8c) = 3 pi R/(2c), half of 3 pi R/c. The nonintegrability statements are those of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (c). (c) is the Omega = 0 substitution. (d) Scope only. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Bell congruence worked: internal material length gamma(t)L and constant chart separation
items.statement:
Worked computation of the internal material length for the Bell congruence of [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (d) and the material metric of [[lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching]]. Fix $c > 0$ and $\alpha > 0$, let $J := (-c/\alpha, c/\alpha)$, put $q(t) := \frac12 \alpha t^2$ on $J$ and let $x_\xi(t) := x^{-1}(c t, q(t) + \xi, 0, 0)$ for $\xi$ in an open interval containing $[0,L]$, $L > 0$, in the inertial chart $x$ with $x^0 = c t$. Then $|q'(t)| = \alpha|t| < c$ on the two-sided domain $J$; write $\beta(t) := \alpha t/c$ and $\gamma(t) := (1 - \beta(t)^2)^{-1/2}$.

(a) The translated congruence field is $n = \gamma (1, \beta, 0, 0)$ and the material field $e := \partial_\xi$ is the constant $(0,1,0,0)$; since $\eta(n,e) = \gamma \beta$, the $h$-length of $e$ is $|e|_h = \sqrt{\eta(e,e) + \eta(n,e)^2} = \sqrt{1 + \gamma^2 \beta^2} = \gamma(t)$ ([[lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching]] (a), [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (d)). Hence the internal longitudinal material-metric length between labels $0$ and $L$ is $|e|_h L = \gamma(t) L > L$ for every $t \neq 0$, with minimum $L$ at $t = 0$, while the chart-frame separation is $q(t) + L - q(t) = L$ for every $t$ in $J$.

(b) The longitudinal expansion of the translated congruence is $\theta(s,s) = \gamma^3 q' q''/c^3 = \gamma^3 \alpha^2 t/c^3$, with unit rest vector $s = \gamma(\beta,1,0,0)$ ([[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (d)); it vanishes at $t = 0$ and is nonzero for every $t \neq 0$, negative for $t < 0$ and positive for $t > 0$. By [[lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching]] (b) the internal longitudinal material metric component is $G_{11} = h(e,e) = \gamma(t)^2$ and its derivatives in geometric proper length $\sigma = c \tau$ are $d/d\sigma G_{11} = 2 \theta(e,e)$ and $d/d\tau G_{11} = 2 c \theta(e,e)$; with horizontal unit direction $h(e)/\gamma = s$, equivalently the fractional rate of change of the rest separation per unit proper time is $d/d\tau \log\gamma = c \theta(s,s) = \gamma^3 \alpha^2 t/c^2$, and $d(\gamma L)/d \tau = \gamma^4 L \alpha^2 t/c^2$.

(c) Explicit check at $\alpha t = 3c/5$, i.e. $t = 3c/(5\alpha)$ in $J$: $\beta = 3/5$, $\gamma = 5/4$ and $\sinh$ and $\cosh$ are not needed; the rest separation is $5L/4 > L$, the internal metric component is $G_{11} = 25/16 > 1$, the expansion is $\theta(s,s) = (125/64)(3\alpha/(5c^2)) = 75\alpha/(64c^2)$, and using [L7], the fractional rest-separation rate is $c \theta(s,s) = 75\alpha/(64c)$. At $t = 0$ the rest separation takes its minimum $L$ and the expansion vanishes; the domain is the two-sided interval $(-c/\alpha, c/\alpha)$, so both the decelerating branch $t < 0$ (negative expansion) and the accelerating branch $t > 0$ (positive expansion) are included.

(d) **Scope.** The length $\gamma(t)L$ is the integral of the local rest metric over the material-label segment at common flow parameter; no finite endpoint-hyperplane distance is inferred. The computation is exact kinematics of the specified family: it uses no elasticity, no material failure criterion, no force law, no measurement and no empirical claim, and it draws no conclusion about real threads; no choice principle is used.
items.strategy: First use the full material family rather than a one-label-only domain: set tau(t)=integral_0^t gamma(v)^(-1)dv, sigma=c tau and Phi(sigma,xi,y,z)=(ct(sigma),q(t(sigma))+xi,y,z) with (xi,y,z) in an open subset of R^3 containing the prescribed endpoint labels and transverse zero labels. The positive derivative tauprime=1/gamma and the inverse argument in [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]] give a C2 inverse (smooth here by repeating the derivative bootstrap with polynomial q), dt/dsigma=gamma/c, partial_sigma Phi=n, and four independent derivative columns. Thus [[lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching]] applies exactly before restriction to y=z=0. Direct evaluation of the family in the two-sided subluminal domain. (a) Differentiating the members with the chain rule gives tangent (c, q'(t), 0, 0) = (c/gamma) n, so the flow field is n = gamma(1, beta, 0, 0) and each member is future timelike (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition, thm-chain-rule); the h-length computation is eta(e,e) = 1 and eta(n,e) = gamma beta, whence h(e,e) = 1 + gamma^2 beta^2 = gamma^2 (1 - beta^2 + beta^2) = gamma^2 by gamma^{-2} = 1 - beta^2 (def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics (a), lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching (a)). (b) The expansion formula is clause (d) of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples; the material-metric statements are clauses (b) and (c) of lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching applied to e, with theta(e,e) = gamma^2 theta(s,s) because h(e) = gamma s and theta is horizontal, although e/gamma generally differs from s. The logarithmic rate identity follows from d/dtau = gamma d/dt (while d/dsigma = (gamma/c) d/dt for sigma = c tau) and d gamma/dt = gamma^3 beta beta' = gamma^3 q'q''/c^2 (thm-chain-rule, def-derivative). (c) Substituting alpha t = 3c/5 gives beta = 3/5, gamma^{-2} = 1 - 9/25 = 16/25, gamma = 5/4, gamma^2 = 25/16, and theta(s,s) = gamma^3 alpha^2 t/c^3 = (125/64)(alpha^2 (3c/(5alpha))/c^3) = (125/64)(3alpha/(5c^2)) = 75alpha/(64c^2), so c theta(s,s) = 75alpha/(64c); the remaining values are substitutions. (d) Scope only. No choice principle is used.
